title: The task
body: Compress **"aaabcc"**. Index `i` marks where the current run starts, index `j` scans ahead to find where it ends, and `out` collects the pieces.

title: Start the first run
body: The first run starts at index 0 with the character `a`. `j` starts at the same place.

title: Find the end of the run
body: `j` moves forward while it sees `a`, and stops at index 3, the first `b`. The run covers indexes 0 to 2, so its length is j - i = **3**.
code: while (j < s.length && s[j] === s[i]) j++; // j = 3

predict.question: `j` stopped at index 3 and `i` is 0. How long is the run of a's?
predict.explanation: The run covers indexes 0, 1, and 2. The length is j - i = 3 - 0 = 3, because j points one past the last a.

title: Write the piece
body: Add `a` and `3` to `out`, then start the next run where `j` stopped: `i = 3`. Pushing to an array is O(1); we do not build the string yet.
code:
out.push(s[i], String(j - i)); // out = ["a", "3"]
i = j;

title: A run of one
body: `j` moves once and stops at the first `c`. The run of `b` has length 1, so we add `b` and `1`, and the next run starts at index 4.

title: The last run
body: `j` moves past both c's and reaches the end of the message (index 6). The run still has to be written: `c` and `2`.

predict.question: `j` has reached the end of the message. What should happen to the run of c's?
predict.explanation: The end of the message also ends a run. Forgetting the last run is the most common bug in this problem.

title: Join once
body: Join the pieces into **"a3b1c2"**. Each character was visited once by `j`, so the work is **O(n) time**, and the pieces and result take **O(n) space**.
